  "text": "He wiped his thumb before opening the flap. The gum had gone yellow and held a thread from somebody's sleeve.

The first photograph was of a car neither of them remembered. A man stood beside it with his hat in his hand.

“That's not ours,” she said.

“No.”

“Put it aside, though.”

Under it was the garden. He passed it to her by the edges.

There were sheets on the line, and beyond them the pear tree, supported by the forked prop her father had cut. At the bottom of the picture a child's shoe entered the frame.

“You,” she said.

“Could be.”

“I bought those shoes. You wouldn't have the brown.”

He leaned closer. She held the photograph between them, tilting it away from the window's glare.

“I thought the tree was nearer the house.”

“It grew.”

“Not nearer, it didn't.”

She gave a small laugh and laid the picture face down. On the back, in pencil, someone had written June. Nothing else.

He took out the receipt. The paper had split along a fold, separating the price from the name of the shop.

“Your father used to say they'd come for it.”

“Did they?”

“No. Two men came about the roof once. I thought it was them.”

The clock made a dry sound, as though preparing to strike, but did not.

She reached for the garden again.

“There's another envelope,” he said.

“In the bag?”

He nodded.

She studied the little shoe. Then she put the photograph against the sugar bowl, where both of them could see it.

“Finish your bread first,” she said."
